1: ---
2: title: README Template and Selection Guide
3: description: Concise guidance for project, skill, feature and component README files, with routing to the code-folder README template when developer topology is the main need.
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "readme selection guide"
6:   - "project readme template"
7:   - "skill readme routing"
8:   - "narrative readme structure"
9: importance_tier: normal
10: contextType: general
11: version: 1.2.1.0
12: ---
13: 
14: # README Template and Selection Guide
15: 
16: Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text
35: Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |
64: 
65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE
70: 
71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.
72: 
73: | Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
80: | Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
81: | Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
82: | FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |
83: 
84: Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.
85: 
86: ```markdown
87: ## 1. OVERVIEW
88: 
89: [Section content]
90: 
91: ```
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:
110: 
111: ```markdown
112: **`spec.md`**
113: - What the feature is and why it exists.
114: - Required at every level.
115: ```
116: 
117: Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.
118: 
119: Voice by README type:
120: 
121: | Type | Voice |
122: |---|---|
123: | Project, Skill, Feature | Plain explanation first, reference detail later |
124: | Component | Technical and concise |
125: | Code Folder | Technical and concise, via `readme-code-template.md` |
126: 
127: Human Voice Rules apply to all README content:
128: 
129: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.
130: - No semicolons. Split the sentence or use "and".
131: - No Oxford comma in inline lists.
132: - No setup phrases.
133: - No banned words from the HVR reference.
134: - Prefer active voice and direct verbs.
135: 
136: Full reference: [`hvr-rules.md`](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md).
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 5. FRONTMATTER
141: 
142: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.
143: 
144: ```yaml
145: ---
146: title: "[DOCUMENT_TITLE]"
147: description: "[One-sentence description]"
148: trigger_phrases:
149:   - "[search phrase]"
150:   - "[routing phrase]"
151: ---
152: ```
153: 
154: Use frontmatter when it improves routing, search or maintenance. Omit it for small human-only documents.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 6. FILLABLE SCAFFOLD
159: 
160: Copy this scaffold, then remove sections that do not apply.
161: 
162: ````markdown
163: ---
164: title: "[PROJECT_OR_FEATURE_NAME]"
165: description: "[One-sentence description]"
166: trigger_phrases:
167:   - "[search phrase]"
168: version: 1.0.0.0
169: ---
170: 
171: # [PROJECT_OR_FEATURE_NAME]
172: 
173: > [One-sentence purpose statement.]
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 1. OVERVIEW
178: 
179: [Explain what this is, who it is for and why it exists.]
180: 
181: ### Key Statistics
182: 
183: | Metric | Value |
184: |---|---|
185: | Status | [Current state] |
186: | Version | [Version or release channel] |
187: | Main audience | [Who uses this] |
188: | Operating modes | [Mode count or short list] |
189: 
190: ### How This Compares
191: 
192: | Capability | This Project | Related Option |
193: |---|---|---|
194: | [Capability] | [Current behavior] | [Difference] |
195: 
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 2. QUICK START
200: 
201: ```bash
202: # Install or prepare
203: [command]
204: 
205: # Verify
206: [command]
207: ```
208: 
209: Expected result: [what success looks like].
210: 
211: 
212: ---
213: 
214: ## 3. FEATURES
215: 
216: ### Key Features
217: 
218: | Feature | What It Does |
219: |---|---|
220: | [Feature] | [Current behavior] |
221: 
222: 
223: ---
224: 
225: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
226: 
227: | Requirement | Minimum | Notes |
228: |---|---|---|
229: | [Runtime or tool] | [Version] | [Why it is needed] |
230: 
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 5. STRUCTURE
235: 
236: ```text
237: [root]/
238: +-- [path]/        # [Purpose]
239: `-- [file]         # [Purpose]
240: ```
241: 
242: | Path | Purpose |
243: |---|---|
244: | `[path]` | [Role] |
245: 
246: <!-- For items needing more than one line, use the itemized pattern
247:      from Section 4 instead of this table. -->
248: 
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 6. CONFIGURATION
253: 
254: | Option | Default | Purpose |
255: |---|---|---|
256: | `[OPTION]` | `[value]` | [What it controls] |
257: 
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## 7. USAGE EXAMPLES
262: 
263: ```bash
264: [command]
265: ```
266: 
267: Result: [expected output or behavior].
268: 
269: 
270: ---
271: 
272: ## 8. TROUBLESHOOTING
273: 
274: | What You See | Cause | Fix |
275: |---|---|---|
276: | [Symptom] | [Cause] | [Action] |
277: 
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 9. FAQ
282: 
283: **Q: [Question readers ask often]?**
284: 
285: A: [Short answer with a link when useful.]
286: 
287: 
288: ---
289: 
290: ## 10. RELATED RESOURCES
291: 
292: ### Related Skills
293: 
294: | Skill | Relationship | Use When |
295: |---|---|---|
296: | [`[skill-name]`](../skill-name/SKILL.md) | [Sibling or dependency] | [When to use it] |
297: 
298: ### Related Documents
299: 
300: | Document | Purpose |
301: |---|---|
302: | [`[Document]`](./path/to/doc.md) | [Why it matters] |
303: 
304: ````
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## 7. VALIDATION CHECKLIST
309: 
310: - [ ] README type is correct. Code folders use `readme-code-template.md`.
311: - [ ] Included sections match the audience and task.
312: - [ ] No empty sections remain.
313: - [ ] Commands were tested or marked as examples.
314: - [ ] Links use correct relative paths.
315: - [ ] Frontmatter is valid if present.
316: - [ ] No Table of Contents and no `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments.
317: - [ ] HVR passes: no em dashes, semicolons, banned words or setup phrases.
318: 
319: ---
320: 
321: ## 8. RELATED RESOURCES
322: 
323: - [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) - Code-folder README scaffold.
324: - [`SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) - README workflow and reference map.
325: - [`core-standards.md`](../../shared/references/core-standards.md) - Markdown formatting rules.
326: - [`validation.md`](../../shared/references/validation.md) - Document validation and DQI scoring.
327: - [`hvr-rules.md`](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md) - Human Voice Rules.

53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |

65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).

69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE

71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.

74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |

95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:
110: 
111: ```markdown
112: **`spec.md`**
113: - What the feature is and why it exists.
114: - Required at every level.
115: ```

117: Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.

121: | Type | Voice |
122: |---|---|
123: | Project, Skill, Feature | Plain explanation first, reference detail later |
124: | Component | Technical and concise |
125: | Code Folder | Technical and concise, via `readme-code-template.md` |

127: Human Voice Rules apply to all README content:
128: 
129: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.
130: - No semicolons. Split the sentence or use "and".
131: - No Oxford comma in inline lists.
132: - No setup phrases.
133: - No banned words from the HVR reference.
134: - Prefer active voice and direct verbs.

15: # Sketchy Filter (hand-drawn variant)
16: 
17: Optional displacement filter that wobbles every stroke and edge slightly — turns any minimal variant into a hand-drawn "editorial" register without changing layout.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Use when the diagram accompanies an essay rather than technical docs.
24: 
25: ### Grammar
26: 
27: ```svg
28: <defs>
29:   <filter id="sketchy" x="-2%" y="-2%" width="104%" height="104%">
30:     <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.02" numOctaves="2" seed="4"/>
31:     <feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" scale="1.5"/>
32:   </filter>
33: </defs>
34: 
35: <!-- Apply to a group wrapping shapes — NOT text -->
36: <g filter="url(#sketchy)">
37:   <!-- rects, paths, circles, lines go here -->
38: </g>
39: 
40: <!-- Text sits OUTSIDE the filtered group — legibility stays crisp -->
41: <text ...>Labels go here</text>
42: ```
43: 
44: ### Tuning
45: 
46: | Parameter | Range | Effect |
47: |---|---|---|
48: | `baseFrequency` | 0.01–0.04 | Lower = lazy wavy lines; higher = jittery. 0.02 default. |
49: | `numOctaves` | 1–3 | More = more noise detail. 2 is plenty. |
50: | `scale` | 1–6 | 1 barely-there, 1.5 default, 2 visible, 4+ cartoon. |
51: | `seed` | integer | Swap for a different random pattern. |
52: 
53: ### Critical rule
54: 
55: Filter shapes, NOT text. Displacement-mapped text becomes illegible. Structure your SVG so text is in a sibling group outside the filtered group.
56: 
57: ### When to use
58: 
59: - Essay / blog post / newsletter where the diagram is the hero of a narrative page.
60: - "Working sketch" register — showing something is mid-thought, not final architecture.
61: 
62: ### When not to use
63: 
64: - Technical documentation (precision matters).
65: - Diagrams with dense labels or tight alignments (filter reads as noise).
66: - Dark variants — wobble reads as artifact on dark backgrounds. Test first.

16: # Architecture
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** system overviews, data-flow diagrams, integration maps, infra topology.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
25: - Group components by tier or trust boundary (frontend → backend → data; public → private).
26: - Primary flow runs left→right or top→down. Pick one and hold it.
27: - Draw arrows before boxes so z-order puts connections behind components.
28: - 1–2 coral focal nodes: the primary integration point, the primary data store, or the key decision node.
29: - Dashed boundary rectangles mark regions (VPC, security group, trust zone); labels sit on a paper-colored mask over the boundary line.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 3. CONNECTOR STYLE
34: 
35: **Rounded right-angle (orthogonal) connectors are MANDATORY** for all non-horizontal/vertical connections — diagonal `<line>` between off-axis nodes is a hard fail (see SKILL.md §4 Mandatory connector rules). Two-bend elbow path with `r=8`:
36: 
37: ```svg
38: <!-- right+down: from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2), mid = (x1+x2)/2 -->
39: <path d="M x1,y1 H mid-8 Q mid,y1 mid,y1+8 V y2-8 Q mid,y2 mid+8,y2 H x2"
40:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="1.2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
41: ```
42: 
43: Flip the vertical signs for right+up. Use a plain `<line>` only when endpoints share the same x or y. Arrow labels sit on the vertical segment, centered horizontally on `mid` and vertically between the two corners.
44: 
45: **Port selection — use top/bottom for vertical connectors.** When the destination is noticeably above or below the source, exit the source's top/bottom edge and enter the destination's top/bottom edge. Use a single-bend L-path (horizontal → corner → vertical into the node), not a left/right side port:
46: 
47: ```svg
48: <!-- entering a node from its bottom (destination above source) -->
49: <path d="M x1,y_src H x2-8 Q x2,y_src x2,y_src-8 V y_dst"
50:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="1.2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
51: ```
52: 
53: Reserve left/right ports for connections that travel primarily horizontally. Entering a node from the side on a mainly-vertical path looks like the arrow punctures the node face rather than arriving from above or below.
54: 
55: **Dashed paths — same routing rules.** Optional, return, async, and passive flows use `stroke-dasharray="4,3"` and a lighter stroke weight (`stroke-width="1"`). Apply the **same orthogonal routing, port-selection, and bridge/hop rules** as solid paths — the dash pattern only communicates semantic weight, not a different routing grammar. When a dashed path and a solid path must cross, bridge the dashed one (it is by definition the less important connection).
56: 
57: **Zone label margin.** Leave ≥16px between the bottom of the zone eyebrow label and the top of the first enclosed node. Size the zone rect tall enough to contain this header gap (zone `y` = node_top − 32; label mask `y` = zone_y + 4).
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## 4. CROSSING ARROWS — BRIDGE / HOP
62: 
63: When two orthogonal arrows must cross, add a small arc (hop/bridge) on the **less important** arrow at the crossing point. The more important arrow is drawn uninterrupted.
64: 
65: ```svg
66: <!-- Horizontal hop over a vertical crossing at x=cx, on a line at y -->
67: <path d="M x1,y H cx-8 a 8,8 0 0,1 16,0 H x2"
68:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="1.2" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
69: ```
70: 
71: `a 8,8 0 0,1 16,0` is an SVG arc: rx=ry=8, large-arc=0, sweep=1 (curves visually upward), advancing 16px right — creating an 8px-radius semicircular bump over the crossing. For a vertical hop over a horizontal, use `a 8,8 0 0,0 0,16` on the vertical path.
72: 
73: Decide which arrow to bridge: bridge the one that is less semantically important (passive, secondary, write-back), or the one with lighter stroke weight (dashed, muted). Never bridge both.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 5. ZONE GROUPING
78: 
79: Group 2+ nodes that serve the same tier or trust boundary with a zone rect — drawn **before** arrows and nodes (z-order: bg → zones → arrows → nodes):
80: 
81: ```svg
82: <rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="8"
83:       fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.02)" stroke="rgba(45,49,66,0.10)" stroke-width="0.8"/>
84: <rect x="{label_x}" y="{y+4}" width="{label_w}" height="12" rx="2" fill="{paper}"/>
85: <text x="{label_cx}" y="{y+13}" fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.40)" font-size="7"
86:       font-family="'Geist Mono', monospace" text-anchor="middle" letter-spacing="0.14em">LAYER</text>
87: ```
88: 
89: Rules:
90: - Leave 12–16px above the first enclosed node — the eyebrow label sits in this margin.
91: - Zone fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.02)` (2% ink wash). Any stronger competes with node fills.
92: - Max 3 zones per diagram. More and it reads like a swimlane (use that type instead).
93: - Dark mode: swap `rgba(45,49,66,…)` → `rgba(245,245,245,…)` same opacities; label mask fill = `paper` (dark).
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 6. ANTI-PATTERNS
98: - Every box in coral ("this is important too") — hierarchy collapses.
99: - Bidirectional arrow when one direction is obvious from context.
100: - Legend floating inside the diagram area.
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 7. EXAMPLES
105: - `assets/diagrams/architecture.html` — minimal light
106: - `assets/diagrams/architecture-dark.html` — minimal dark
107: - `assets/diagrams/architecture-full.html` — full editorial

16: # Bar / Column Chart
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** comparing discrete quantities across categories or time intervals — sprint velocity, monthly revenue, feature adoption, cohort counts. Use when each category has a single numeric value and the comparison between bars is the primary message.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
25: 
26: - **Orientation:** Vertical bars (columns) are default. Horizontal bars are appropriate when category labels are long or you have more than 8 categories.
27: - **Plot area margins:** left 80px (y-axis labels), bottom 60px (x-axis labels), top 40px, right 40px — inside a `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
28: - **Bar count cap:** 4–8 bars. More than 8 → group into periods or split into two charts.
29: - **Bar width:** ≥ 50% of the column pitch (the gap should never exceed the bar). Typical: pitch=110px, bar=72px.
30: - **Y-axis gridlines:** 4–6 horizontal lines at regular intervals. Stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.08)` (very faint), 0.8px. X-axis baseline at `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)`, 1px.
31: - **Y-axis labels:** right-aligned Geist Mono 8px muted, at x=72 (8px left of the plot area).
32: - **X-axis labels:** centered below each bar, Geist sans 11px 600 for category names.
33: - **Value labels:** Geist Mono 8px above each bar. Focal bar label in accent; others in muted.
34: - **Focal bar:** 1 bar max in accent fill/stroke. All others in `muted @ 0.15` fill + `muted` stroke.
35: - **Y-axis line:** thin vertical `<line>` at x=80 from y=40 to y=420.
36: 
37: ### Bar element pattern
38: 
39: ```svg
40: <!-- Opaque paper mask prevents bleed from background -->
41: <rect x="X" y="Y" width="W" height="H" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
42: <!-- Bar body -->
43: <rect x="X" y="Y" width="W" height="H" fill="rgba(79,93,117,0.15)" stroke="#4f5d75" stroke-width="1"/>
44: <!-- Value label above bar -->
45: <text x="X+W/2" y="Y-8" fill="#4f5d75" font-size="8" font-family="'Geist Mono', monospace" text-anchor="middle">VALUE</text>
46: ```
47: 
48: Focal bar: replace fill with `rgba(235,108,54,0.12)`, stroke with `#eb6c36`, label fill with `#eb6c36`.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
53: 
54: - More than 8 bars without grouping (illegible at normal scale).
55: - Truncated y-axis (not starting at 0) — distorts the magnitude comparison.
56: - Accent on more than 1 bar ("everything is important" = nothing is).

16: # Bar / Column Chart
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** comparing discrete quantities across categories or time intervals — sprint velocity, monthly revenue, feature adoption, cohort counts. Use when each category has a single numeric value and the comparison between bars is the primary message.
21:

23: 
24: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
25: 
26: - **Orientation:** Vertical bars (columns) are default. Horizontal bars are appropriate when category labels are long or you have more than 8 categories.
27: - **Plot area margins:** left 80px (y-axis labels), bottom 60px (x-axis labels), top 40px, right 40px — inside a `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
28: - **Bar count cap:** 4–8 bars. More than 8 → group into periods or split into two charts.
29: - **Bar width:** ≥ 50% of the column pitch (the gap should never exceed the bar). Typical: pitch=110px, bar=72px.
30: - **Y-axis gridlines:** 4–6 horizontal lines at regular intervals. Stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.08)` (very faint), 0.8px. X-axis baseline at `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)`, 1px.
31: - **Y-axis labels:** right-aligned Geist Mono 8px muted, at x=72 (8px left of the plot area).
32: - **X-axis labels:** centered below each bar, Geist sans 11px 600 for category names.
33: - **Value labels:** Geist Mono 8px above each bar. Focal bar label in accent; others in muted.
34: - **Focal bar:** 1 bar max in accent fill/stroke. All others in `muted @ 0.15` fill + `muted` stroke.
35: - **Y-axis line:** thin vertical `<line>` at x=80 from y=40 to y=420.
36: 
37: ### Bar element pattern
38: 
39: ```svg
40: <!-- Opaque paper mask prevents bleed from background -->
41: <rect x="X" y="Y" width="W" height="H" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
42: <!-- Bar body -->
43: <rect x="X" y="Y" width="W" height="H" fill="rgba(79,93,117,0.15)" stroke="#4f5d75" stroke-width="1"/>
44: <!-- Value label above bar -->
45: <text x="X+W/2" y="Y-8" fill="#4f5d75" font-size="8" font-family="'Geist Mono', monospace" text-anchor="middle">VALUE</text>
46: ```
47: 
48: Focal bar: replace fill with `rgba(235,108,54,0.12)`, stroke with `#eb6c36`, label fill with `#eb6c36`.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
53: 
54: - More than 8 bars without grouping (illegible at normal scale).
55: - Truncated y-axis (not starting at 0) — distorts the magnitude comparison.
56: - Accent on more than 1 bar ("everything is important" = nothing is).
57: - 3-D bar extrusion — no shadows, no depth.
58: - Category labels rotated more than 45°; prefer short labels or horizontal chart instead.

64: - **Grouped bars:** two bars per category, side by side. Use `accent` for the primary series and `series-1` for the secondary. Max 2 groups.

16: # Data Flow
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** visualising how data moves through a pipeline *across organisational roles* — who initiates, who processes, who publishes, and who consumes. The canonical use case is a multi-role data platform (Admin → Engineers → Scientists → Consumers) with 4–6 process steps. Use when the reader needs to understand **who does what at each stage**, not just the technical components.
21: 
22: Prefer standard **Swimlane** for cross-functional business processes (HR approvals, support tickets). Use **Data flow** when the subject is a data pipeline with typed payloads (raw files, tables, reports) and role-scoped access boundaries.
23: 
24: This type is **parametric** — the inputs schema in §2 drives every coordinate via the formulas in §3. Two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
29: 
30: ```yaml
31: lanes:                              # 1..4 horizontal swimlanes (top to bottom)
32:   - { name: ["DATA", "ADMINS"],     key: "ADM" }
33:   - { name: ["DATA", "ENGINEERS"],  key: "ENG" }
34:   - { name: ["DATA", "SCIENTISTS"], key: "SCI" }
35:   - { name: ["DATA", "CONSUMERS"],  key: "CON" }
36: 
37: steps:                              # 1..6 columns (left to right)
38:   - { number: "01", label: "COLLECT" }
39:   - { number: "02", label: "STORE" }
40:   - { number: "03", label: "TRANSFORM" }
41:   - { number: "04", label: "ANALYZE",  focal: true }   # focal step header chip — accent fill
42:   - { number: "05", label: "PUBLISH" }
43: 
44: nodes:                              # explicit per-cell entries; empty cells render nothing
45:   - { lane: "ADM", step: 0, title: "Project Setup",   sub: "create · assign roles",     tool: "Platform console" }
46:   - { lane: "ADM", step: 1, title: "Access Control",  sub: "bucket policies · LDAP",    tool: "MinIO · LDAP console",
47:       color: "#b85450" }            # tinted rust-red to flag governance/identity concern
48:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 0, title: "Source Ingest",   sub: "ext. sources → raw",        tool: "NiFi · API · SFTP",
49:       chips: {in: "WB", out: "DB"} }                    # web payload in, dataset out
50:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 1, title: "Raw Store",       sub: "raw landing zones",         tool: "MinIO raw",
51:       chips: {in: "DB", out: "DB"} }                    # raw stays raw inside the landing zone
52:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 2, title: "Clean & Stage",   sub: "raw → staging → anon",      tool: "NiFi · Trino",
53:       chips: {in: "DB", out: "TB"} }                    # raw dataset → analysis-ready table
54:   - { lane: "SCI", step: 3, title: "Explore & Model", sub: "anon data → insights",      tool: "JupyterHub · Trino",
55:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "FL"}, focal: true }       # focal — table in, file/report out
56:   - { lane: "SCI", step: 4, title: "Publish Findings", sub: "models → dashboards",      tool: "Superset · Reports",
57:       chips: {in: "FL", out: "FL"} }                    # report in, report out (pass-through to publish)
58:   - { lane: "CON", step: 4, title: "Query Insights",   sub: "aggregated views",         tool: "Trino (read-only)",
59:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "TB"} }                    # consumers read tables, hand off tables
60: 
61: arrows:                             # explicit edges; styles bind to topology (see §4)
62:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ADM", step: 1}, style: "muted" }
63:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 0}, style: "trigger" }   # dashed governance
64:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 1}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, style: "trigger" }
65:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, style: "muted" }
66:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 2}, style: "muted" }
67:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 2}, to: {lane: "SCI", step: 3}, style: "accent",     # focal cross-role
68:       label: "anon data" }
69:   - { from: {lane: "SCI", step: 3}, to: {lane: "SCI", step: 4}, style: "muted" }
70:   - { from: {lane: "SCI", step: 4}, to: {lane: "CON", step: 4}, style: "link" }     # teal: published
71: 
72: dark: false
73: ```
74: 
75: **Reserved field semantics:**
76: - `lanes[k].key` — the 3-letter role chip text (e.g., `ADM`, `ENG`, `SCI`, `CON`). Used inside every node in that lane.
77: - `lanes[k].name` — two-line lane label; both lines use the uppercase `eyebrow` role.
78: - `steps[j].focal: true` — exactly **one** step may declare this. Header chip renders in accent.
79: - `nodes[i].focal: true` — exactly **one** node may declare this. Renders with accent border (§6).
80: - `nodes[i].chips` — data-type chips for the node. Either form accepted:
81:   - **Object form (preferred):** `{in: "<CODE>", out: "<CODE>"}` — explicit input/output semantic. Either side optional.
82:   - **Array form:** `["<INPUT_CODE>", "<OUTPUT_CODE>"]` — first item is input, second is output.
83:   - Codes from §9 (`WB`, `DB`, `TB`, `FL`, `LS`). Position is **fixed**: input chip on the node's bottom-**left**, output chip on the bottom-**right**.
84: - `nodes[i].color` — optional **per-node color override**. Any valid `"#hex"` string is accepted; the §5 palette is recommended for cross-diagram consistency but not required. Every node can carry its own color independently of others.
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
89: 
90: ```
91: label_col_w      = 140
92: step_slot_w      = 112
93: right_pad        = 28
94: n_steps          = len(steps)
95: n_lanes          = len(lanes)
96: 
97: # Canvas
98: viewBox_w        = label_col_w + n_steps * step_slot_w + right_pad   # 5 steps → 728
99: header_h         = 36
100: lane_h           = 80
101: has_color_row    = any(node.color or step.color or lane.color in inputs)
102: legend_h         = 100 if has_color_row else 80                      # 4 rows when colors are present
103: viewBox_h        = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h + legend_h            # 4 lanes, no colors → 436; with colors → 456
104: 
105: # Header strip (top)
106: header_y         = 0                                                  # ends at header_h = 36
107: step_chip_y      = 6                                                  # 16-px chip at y=6..22
108: step_label_y     = 29                                                 # text line below chip
109: 
110: # Lane positions
111: lane_y_top(k)    = header_h + k * lane_h                              # 36, 116, 196, 276
112: lane_y_mid(k)    = lane_y_top(k) + lane_h/2                           # 76, 156, 236, 316
113: lane_label_x     = label_col_w / 2                                    # 70
114: 
115: # Step / node center x
116: step_cx(j)       = label_col_w + j * step_slot_w + step_slot_w/2      # 196, 308, 420, 532, 644
117: 
118: # Nodes
119: node_w           = 100
120: node_h           = 64
121: node_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - node_w/2                              # 146, 258, 370, 482, 594
122: node_y(k)        = lane_y_top(k) + 8                                  # 44, 124, 204, 284
123: 
124: # Legend strip (bottom)
125: legend_y_top     = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h                        # 356
126: legend_row_y     = [legend_y_top + 16, legend_y_top + 37, legend_y_top + 59]
127:                                                                       # 372, 393, 415
128: ```
129: 
130: ### 3.1 Background structure
131: 
132: - Paper fill across full viewBox.
133: - Dot pattern: 22×22 grid, `circle r=0.8`, `fill ink @ 0.10`.
134: - Alternating lane tints: odd-indexed lanes (0, 2, …) receive `ink @ 0.018` fill.
135: - Lane dividers: horizontal hairlines at every `lane_y_top(k)` and at `legend_y_top`, stroke `ink @ 0.12` width 0.8.
136: - Label column right border: vertical hairline at `x = label_col_w`, from `y = header_h` to `y = legend_y_top`.
137: 
138: ### 3.2 Step header chip
139: 
140: Per step `j`:
141: 
142: ```
143: chip_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - 16        # 16×16 chip
144: chip_y           = 6
145: chip_w           = 32
146: chip_h           = 16
147: chip_rx          = 8                       # pill-shaped
148: number_anchor    = (step_cx(j), 14)
149: label_anchor     = (step_cx(j), 29)
150: ```
151: 
152: Default fill: `ink @ 0.12`, number text ink, label text muted.
153: Focal fill: `accent @ 0.20`, number + label text accent.
154: Per-step `color` override (§5): replaces the fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the text fill with `C`.
155: 
156: ### 3.3 Lane labels
157: 
158: Two-line `eyebrow` role label, both lines uppercase, fill muted:
159: - Line 1 at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) - 4)`
160: - Line 2 at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 8)`
161: 
162: Per-lane `color` override (§5): replaces the label fill with `C` and the lane tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` (instead of the default `ink @ 0.018`).
163: 
164: ### 3.4 Node content layout (inside the 100×64 rect)
165: 
166: ```
167: role_chip          rect 18×10 at (node_x+4, node_y+4),  rx=3
168: role_chip_text     centered at (node_x+13, node_y+9), eyebrow role, font-size=6, weight=600
169: title              centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+23), node-name role, font-size=9
170: sub                centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+35), sublabel role, font-size=6.5, muted
171: tool               centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+47), sublabel role, font-size=6.5, soft
172: data chip IN       rect 16×8 at (node_x+4,   node_y+54), rx=3      # payload type entering the node
173: data chip OUT      rect 16×8 at (node_x+80,  node_y+54), rx=3      # payload type leaving the node
174: ```
175: 
176: Empty cells (no node entry) render **nothing**. No placeholder rect, no role chip, no label — the cell is invisible.
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 4. ARROW RULES (MANDATORY)
181: 
182: Four styles, bound to topology. Connectors are drawn **before** all node rects (z-order rule).
183: 
184: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
185: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
186: | `muted` | `muted` | 1.0 | — | `arr-muted` | Standard data hand-off between steps or within a lane. |
187: | `trigger` | `muted` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arr-muted` | Governance trigger — an admin action enables downstream work. Unlabelled. |
188: | `accent` | `accent` | 1.2 | — | `arr-accent` | Focal cross-role handoff. **Exactly one per diagram**, labeled. |
189: | `link` | `link` | 1.0 | — | `arr-link` | Published / externally-consumed output. |
190: 
191: **Defs block** (required, three markers):
192: 
193: ```svg
194: <defs>
195:   <pattern id="dots" width="22" height="22" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
196:     <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="0.8" fill="{ink @ 0.10}"/>
197:   </pattern>
198:   <marker id="arr-muted"  markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{muted}"/></marker>
199:   <marker id="arr-accent" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{accent}"/></marker>
200:   <marker id="arr-link"   markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{link}"/></marker>
201: </defs>
202: ```
203: 
204: ### 4.1 Routing rules (non-negotiable)
205: 
206: - **Single-bend routing:** horizontal-first, then vertical. Exit a node from the **right edge**; enter from the **left** (same-lane horizontal) or **top/bottom** (cross-lane vertical).
207: - **No diagonals.** Bends use an 8-px Q-bezier corner.
208: - **Same-step cross-lane (vertical)**: line directly between `(step_cx(j), lane_y_top(k_to)−12)` and `(step_cx(j), lane_y_top(k_to))`. Used for admin → engineers triggers under the same step.
209: - **Cross-lane cross-step (focal)**: exit right, run horizontal past the source node's right edge to a corridor x just before the target's step, then drop vertically.
210: - **Labels:** only the `accent` arrow gets a label. Use a paper-filled rect mask (opaque) 6 px behind the text. Other arrows are unlabelled.
211: - **Z-order:** all arrows emitted before any node rect (the rect fills mask the line ends inside the node).
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE
216: 
217: Any node, lane, or step may declare an optional `color: "#hex"`. Mirrors high-level §4.4 and dp-integration §5 so the rule reads identically across types.
218: 
219: ### 5.1 Per-node `color`
220: 
221: Applied to:
222: 
223: | Element | Light | Dark |
224: |---|---|---|
225: | Container fill (`rect`) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
226: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (stroke-width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.45)` |
227: | Role chip fill | `rgba(C, 0.18)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.22)` |
228: | Role chip text | `C` | `C_light` |
229: | Title text | `C` | `C_light` |
230: | Sub-label | **unchanged** (muted) | **unchanged** (muted) |
231: | Tool label | **unchanged** (soft) | **unchanged** (soft) |
232: | Data-type chips | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
233: | Arrows touching this node | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
234: 
235: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15% for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
236: 
237: ### 5.2 Per-step `color`
238: 
239: Replaces the step header chip's fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the chip's number + label text fill with `C`. The legend's matching step entry uses the same colors.
240: 
241: ### 5.3 Per-lane `color`
242: 
243: Replaces the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` (only for odd-indexed lanes that receive a tint by default — or extend to all lanes if explicitly chosen) and the lane label text fill with `C`. Use sparingly; lane tints are easy to over-apply.
244: 
245: ### 5.4 Rules
246: 
247: - **Never on focal nodes / focal steps.** The accent already carries that signal. A `color` on a focal element is ignored.
248: - **Never on arrows.** Arrows are topology-driven. If you want a colored edge, pick a different `style` from §4, not a color override.
249: - **Cap at 3 custom-colored elements** per diagram (nodes + lanes + steps combined), in addition to the focal pair (focal node + focal step header). Above 3 the visual signal starts to fragment — if you need more, split the diagram or rethink whether each color carries distinct meaning.
250: - **Subtitles and tool labels stay muted.** Only the primary identity (border + role chip + title + icon) carries the color signal.
251: 
252: ### 5.5 Semantic palette (recommended)
253: 
254: Same palette as high-level / dp-integration so a reader scanning multiple diagrams sees the same colors meaning the same thing:
255: 
256: - `#b85450` rust-red — Security / Identity / Governance (admin nodes, LDAP, access control)
257: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — Observability / Quality (monitoring, data-quality gates, lineage)
258: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — Governance / Lineage (catalog, metadata)
259: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — Backup / DR / Archive
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
264: 
265: The data-flow diagram is built around **one cross-role handoff** that defines its central claim. Three focal slots, exactly one entry each:
266: 
267: - **One focal step** (`steps[j].focal: true`) — typically the analytical pivot (Analyze, Model, …). Header chip and legend chip both render in accent.
268: - **One focal node** (`nodes[i].focal: true`) — the node that *receives* the focal handoff. Accent border + accent role chip + ink title.
269: - **One focal arrow** (`arrows[i].style: "accent"`) — the cross-role handoff into the focal node. Solid accent stroke + labeled with a short payload descriptor (e.g., `anon data`).
270: 
271: If zero or >1 of any focal slot are declared, halt and ask the user.
272: 
273: ---
274: 
275: ## 7. DARK MODE
276: 
277: | Token | Light | Dark |
278: |---|---|---|
279: | Paper | `paper` | `ink` |
280: | Ink | `ink` | `paper` |
281: | Muted | `muted` | `soft` |
282: | Soft | `soft` | `rule-solid` |
283: | Accent | `accent` | `accent` |
284: | Link | `link` | `link` |
285: | Dot pattern | `ink @ 0.10` | `paper @ 0.10` |
286: | Lane tint | `ink @ 0.018` | `paper @ 0.025` |
287: | Dividers | `ink @ 0.12` | `paper @ 0.12` |
288: | Default chip fill | `ink @ 0.12` | `paper @ 0.12` |
289: | Focal chip fill | `accent @ 0.20` | `accent @ 0.22` |
290: | Default node fill | `paper` | `paper @ 0.04` |
291: | Default node stroke | `ink @ 0.25` | `paper @ 0.20` |
292: | Focal node fill | `accent @ 0.07` | `accent @ 0.12` |
293: | Focal node stroke | `accent` | `accent` |
294: | Custom component colors | `C` | `C_light` (lighten ~15%) |
295: 
296: ---
297: 
298: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
299: 
300: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
301: 
302: 1. `viewBox = "0 0 {viewBox_w} {viewBox_h}"` derived from `n_steps` and `n_lanes` via §3.
303: 2. Header strip at `y=0..36`; legend strip at `y=legend_y_top..viewBox_h` (`legend_y_top = 36 + n_lanes * 80`).
304: 3. Every node at `(step_cx(j) - 50, lane_y_top(k) + 8)` size `100×64`.
305: 4. Empty cells render nothing — no placeholder rect, no text.
306: 5. Exactly **one** focal step (`steps[j].focal: true`).
307: 6. Exactly **one** focal node (`nodes[i].focal: true`).
308: 7. Exactly **one** focal arrow (`style: accent`). Labeled, with a paper-masked rect behind the label.
309: 8. All other arrows unlabelled.
310: 9. All arrows emitted before any node rect (z-order rule).
311: 10. Single-bend routing only — no diagonals. Q-bezier `r=8` at each bend.
312: 11. Custom component colors ≤ 3 (in addition to the focal pair). Arrows never recolored by component `color`.
313: 12. Subtitle and tool labels stay muted regardless of any component `color`.
314: 
315: ---
316: 
317: ## 9. DATA-TYPE CHIPS REFERENCE (INPUT + OUTPUT)
318: 
319: Small `16×8 rx=3` badges at the bottom of each node, one for input and one for output. Position is **non-negotiable**:
320: 
321: - **Input chip** at `(node_x+4, node_y+54)` — bottom-**left** of the node. Represents the payload format *entering* the node from upstream.
322: - **Output chip** at `(node_x+80, node_y+54)` — bottom-**right** of the node. Represents the payload format *leaving* the node toward downstream.
323: 
324: Either chip may be omitted (e.g., a sink node has only an input chip; a source-only node has only an output chip). Reading the diagram becomes a payload-transformation trace: scan a row, read each node's input → output, and you see exactly what shape the data takes at each hand-off.
325: 
326: ### Chip codes
327: 
328: | Code | Color | Meaning |
329: |------|-------|---------|
330: | `WB` | `#6e6479` (mauve) | Web / Public data |
331: | `DB` | `#5c7899` (steel-blue) | Dataset / Raw file |
332: | `TB` | `#b8915a` (amber) | Table / Analysis-ready |
333: | `FL` | `#9c6b50` (sienna) | File / Report / Export |
334: | `LS` | `#4a7c59` (forest) | Live stream / Event |
335: 
336: Text inside chip: white, `eyebrow` role at 5px, weight 700.
337: 
338: Data-type chip colors are a **separate semantic axis** from the per-node color override (§5). The chip colors describe *payload format*; the node color override describes *concern type* (governance, observability, …). Don't conflate them — a node can have both an `out: TB` amber chip and a rust-red border color simultaneously.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## 10. LEGEND (3- OR 4-ROW STRIP)
343: 
344: Each row introduced by a category label at `x=144`. The default legend has **3 rows** (`STEPS` / `DATA TYPE` / `FLOW`); when one or more nodes carry a `color` override (§5), add a 4th `CONCERN` row and grow `legend_h` to 100 (so `viewBox_h = header_h + n_lanes·80 + 100`).
345: 
346: - **Row 1 — `STEPS`** at `y = legend_y_top + 16`: repeat the header chips with their labels. Focal step keeps accent fill.
347: - **Row 2 — `DATA TYPE`** at `y = legend_y_top + 37`: one swatch per chip type actually used in the diagram. **Append a small sub-hint** in the muted `sublabel` role after the chips: `left chip = input · right chip = output`. This makes the position-based input/output convention explicit for first-time readers.
348: - **Row 3 — `CONCERN`** (only when color overrides are present) at `y = legend_y_top + 58`: one mini-rect per custom color used, with its semantic label (e.g., `Identity · Governance`, `Data Quality · Observability`). The focal accent swatch is also shown here so the reader sees all three colored axes side-by-side.
349: - **Row 4 — `FLOW`** (last row, position depends on whether `CONCERN` row exists): short line segments with their marker + text label, one per arrow style actually used.
350: 
351: All legend items align on a single horizontal strip per row. Do not stack vertically inside a box.
352: 
353: ---
354: 
355: ## 11. COMPLEXITY BUDGET
356: 
357: | Dimension | Max |
358: |---|---|
359: | Lanes (roles) | 4 |
360: | Steps | 6 |
361: | Nodes per lane | Nodes = active steps only — empty cells are invisible (no placeholder box) |
362: | Labelled arrows | 1 (focal accent only) |
363: | Data-type chips per node | 2 |
364: | Custom-colored elements (§5) | 3 (in addition to focal node + focal step) |
365: 
366: Above 4 lanes or 6 steps: split into two diagrams (e.g., ingestion pipeline / analytics pipeline).
367: 
368: ---
369: 
370: ## 12. ANTI-PATTERNS
371: 
372: - **Placeholder empty cells** — if a role doesn't participate in a step, leave the cell empty (no box, no text).
373: - **More than one labelled arrow** — only the focal cross-role handoff gets a label.
374: - **Diagonal arrows** — always horizontal-first, then vertical; single right-angle bend.
375: - **`title` role for node titles** — node titles use the `node-name` role (technical context). Only the page `<h1>` uses `title`.
376: - **Accent on more than one node, one step, one arrow** — focal = one node + one step + one arrow, max.
377: - **`node-name` role for role labels** — lane labels always use the uppercase `eyebrow` role (they are identifiers, not prose).
378: - **`color` override on a focal element** — ignored. Accent always wins.
379: - **Custom-colored arrows** — arrows are topology-driven. Color on a node never spreads to its edges.
380: - **Lane tints over-applied** — a tint on every lane reads as decoration, not signal. Apply to ≤1 lane.
381: 
382: ---
383: 
384: ## 13. EXAMPLES
385: 
386: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow.html` — minimal light (the platform, 4-role × 5-step: Admin, Engineers, Scientists, Consumers). Gallery default.
387: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-dark.html` — same, dark skin.
388: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-full.html` — same, editorial-card frame.
389: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended.html` — exercises §5 color override: Access Control node in rust-red (governance), Clean & Stage node in slate-blue (data quality). Focal accent on Analyze step + Explore & Model node + anon-data arrow unchanged.
390: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended-dark.html` — extended pattern, dark skin.
391: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended-full.html` — extended pattern, editorial-card frame.

2: title: "Data Flow"
3: description: "Parametric layout for role-scoped data pipelines — lane/step schema, deterministic geometry, data-type chips, arrow styles, and the one-focal-handoff rule."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "data flow diagram"
6:   - "role scoped data pipeline"
7:   - "data pipeline lanes"
8:   - "payload transformation trace"
9:   - "data type chips"
10:   - "cross role handoff"
11: importance_tier: normal
12: contextType: implementation
13: version: 1.2.1.0
14: ---
15: 
16: # Data Flow
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** visualising how data moves through a pipeline *across organisational roles* — who initiates, who processes, who publishes, and who consumes. The canonical use case is a multi-role data platform (Admin → Engineers → Scientists → Consumers) with 4–6 process steps. Use when the reader needs to understand **who does what at each stage**, not just the technical components.
21: 
22: Prefer standard **Swimlane** for cross-functional business processes (HR approvals, support tickets). Use **Data flow** when the subject is a data pipeline with typed payloads (raw files, tables, reports) and role-scoped access boundaries.
23: 
24: This type is **parametric** — the inputs schema in §2 drives every coordinate via the formulas in §3. Two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
29: 
30: ```yaml
31: lanes:                              # 1..4 horizontal swimlanes (top to bottom)
32:   - { name: ["DATA", "ADMINS"],     key: "ADM" }
33:   - { name: ["DATA", "ENGINEERS"],  key: "ENG" }
34:   - { name: ["DATA", "SCIENTISTS"], key: "SCI" }
35:   - { name: ["DATA", "CONSUMERS"],  key: "CON" }
36: 
37: steps:                              # 1..6 columns (left to right)
38:   - { number: "01", label: "COLLECT" }
39:   - { number: "02", label: "STORE" }
40:   - { number: "03", label: "TRANSFORM" }
41:   - { number: "04", label: "ANALYZE",  focal: true }   # focal step header chip — accent fill
42:   - { number: "05", label: "PUBLISH" }
43: 
44: nodes:                              # explicit per-cell entries; empty cells render nothing
45:   - { lane: "ADM", step: 0, title: "Project Setup",   sub: "create · assign roles",     tool: "Platform console" }
46:   - { lane: "ADM", step: 1, title: "Access Control",  sub: "bucket policies · LDAP",    tool: "MinIO · LDAP console",
47:       color: "#b85450" }            # tinted rust-red to flag governance/identity concern
48:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 0, title: "Source Ingest",   sub: "ext. sources → raw",        tool: "NiFi · API · SFTP",
49:       chips: {in: "WB", out: "DB"} }                    # web payload in, dataset out
50:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 1, title: "Raw Store",       sub: "raw landing zones",         tool: "MinIO raw",
51:       chips: {in: "DB", out: "DB"} }                    # raw stays raw inside the landing zone
52:   - { lane: "ENG", step: 2, title: "Clean & Stage",   sub: "raw → staging → anon",      tool: "NiFi · Trino",
53:       chips: {in: "DB", out: "TB"} }                    # raw dataset → analysis-ready table
54:   - { lane: "SCI", step: 3, title: "Explore & Model", sub: "anon data → insights",      tool: "JupyterHub · Trino",
55:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "FL"}, focal: true }       # focal — table in, file/report out
56:   - { lane: "SCI", step: 4, title: "Publish Findings", sub: "models → dashboards",      tool: "Superset · Reports",
57:       chips: {in: "FL", out: "FL"} }                    # report in, report out (pass-through to publish)
58:   - { lane: "CON", step: 4, title: "Query Insights",   sub: "aggregated views",         tool: "Trino (read-only)",
59:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "TB"} }                    # consumers read tables, hand off tables
60: 
61: arrows:                             # explicit edges; styles bind to topology (see §4)
62:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ADM", step: 1}, style: "muted" }
63:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 0}, style: "trigger" }   # dashed governance
64:   - { from: {lane: "ADM", step: 1}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, style: "trigger" }
65:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 0}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, style: "muted" }
66:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 1}, to: {lane: "ENG", step: 2}, style: "muted" }
67:   - { from: {lane: "ENG", step: 2}, to: {lane: "SCI", step: 3}, style: "accent",     # focal cross-role
68:       label: "anon data" }
69:   - { from: {lane: "SCI", step: 3}, to: {lane: "SCI", step: 4}, style: "muted" }
70:   - { from: {lane: "SCI", step: 4}, to: {lane: "CON", step: 4}, style: "link" }     # teal: published
71: 
72: dark: false
73: ```
74: 
75: **Reserved field semantics:**
76: - `lanes[k].key` — the 3-letter role chip text (e.g., `ADM`, `ENG`, `SCI`, `CON`). Used inside every node in that lane.
77: - `lanes[k].name` — two-line lane label; both lines use the uppercase `eyebrow` role.
78: - `steps[j].focal: true` — exactly **one** step may declare this. Header chip renders in accent.
79: - `nodes[i].focal: true` — exactly **one** node may declare this. Renders with accent border (§6).
80: - `nodes[i].chips` — data-type chips for the node. Either form accepted:
81:   - **Object form (preferred):** `{in: "<CODE>", out: "<CODE>"}` — explicit input/output semantic. Either side optional.
82:   - **Array form:** `["<INPUT_CODE>", "<OUTPUT_CODE>"]` — first item is input, second is output.
83:   - Codes from §9 (`WB`, `DB`, `TB`, `FL`, `LS`). Position is **fixed**: input chip on the node's bottom-**left**, output chip on the bottom-**right**.
84: - `nodes[i].color` — optional **per-node color override**. Any valid `"#hex"` string is accepted; the §5 palette is recommended for cross-diagram consistency but not required. Every node can carry its own color independently of others.
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
89: 
90: ```
91: label_col_w      = 140
92: step_slot_w      = 112
93: right_pad        = 28
94: n_steps          = len(steps)
95: n_lanes          = len(lanes)
96: 
97: # Canvas
98: viewBox_w        = label_col_w + n_steps * step_slot_w + right_pad   # 5 steps → 728
99: header_h         = 36
100: lane_h           = 80
101: has_color_row    = any(node.color or step.color or lane.color in inputs)
102: legend_h         = 100 if has_color_row else 80                      # 4 rows when colors are present
103: viewBox_h        = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h + legend_h            # 4 lanes, no colors → 436; with colors → 456
104: 
105: # Header strip (top)
106: header_y         = 0                                                  # ends at header_h = 36
107: step_chip_y      = 6                                                  # 16-px chip at y=6..22
108: step_label_y     = 29                                                 # text line below chip
109: 
110: # Lane positions
111: lane_y_top(k)    = header_h + k * lane_h                              # 36, 116, 196, 276
112: lane_y_mid(k)    = lane_y_top(k) + lane_h/2                           # 76, 156, 236, 316
113: lane_label_x     = label_col_w / 2                                    # 70
114: 
115: # Step / node center x
116: step_cx(j)       = label_col_w + j * step_slot_w + step_slot_w/2      # 196, 308, 420, 532, 644
117: 
118: # Nodes
119: node_w           = 100
120: node_h           = 64
121: node_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - node_w/2                              # 146, 258, 370, 482, 594
122: node_y(k)        = lane_y_top(k) + 8                                  # 44, 124, 204, 284
123: 
124: # Legend strip (bottom)
125: legend_y_top     = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h                        # 356
126: legend_row_y     = [legend_y_top + 16, legend_y_top + 37, legend_y_top + 59]
127:                                                                       # 372, 393, 415
128: ```
129: 
130: ### 3.1 Background structure
131: 
132: - Paper fill across full viewBox.
133: - Dot pattern: 22×22 grid, `circle r=0.8`, `fill ink @ 0.10`.
134: - Alternating lane tints: odd-indexed lanes (0, 2, …) receive `ink @ 0.018` fill.
135: - Lane dividers: horizontal hairlines at every `lane_y_top(k)` and at `legend_y_top`, stroke `ink @ 0.12` width 0.8.
136: - Label column right border: vertical hairline at `x = label_col_w`, from `y = header_h` to `y = legend_y_top`.
137: 
138: ### 3.2 Step header chip
139: 
140: Per step `j`:
141: 
142: ```
143: chip_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - 16        # 16×16 chip
144: chip_y           = 6
145: chip_w           = 32
146: chip_h           = 16
147: chip_rx          = 8                       # pill-shaped
148: number_anchor    = (step_cx(j), 14)
149: label_anchor     = (step_cx(j), 29)
150: ```
151: 
152: Default fill: `ink @ 0.12`, number text ink, label text muted.
153: Focal fill: `accent @ 0.20`, number + label text accent.
154: Per-step `color` override (§5): replaces the fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the text fill with `C`.
155: 
156: ### 3.3 Lane labels
157: 
158: Two-line `eyebrow` role label, both lines uppercase, fill muted:
159: - Line 1 at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) - 4)`
160: - Line 2 at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 8)`
161: 
162: Per-lane `color` override (§5): replaces the label fill with `C` and the lane tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` (instead of the default `ink @ 0.018`).
163: 
164: ### 3.4 Node content layout (inside the 100×64 rect)
165: 
166: ```
167: role_chip          rect 18×10 at (node_x+4, node_y+4),  rx=3
168: role_chip_text     centered at (node_x+13, node_y+9), eyebrow role, font-size=6, weight=600
169: title              centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+23), node-name role, font-size=9
170: sub                centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+35), sublabel role, font-size=6.5, muted
171: tool               centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+47), sublabel role, font-size=6.5, soft
172: data chip IN       rect 16×8 at (node_x+4,   node_y+54), rx=3      # payload type entering the node
173: data chip OUT      rect 16×8 at (node_x+80,  node_y+54), rx=3      # payload type leaving the node
174: ```
175: 
176: Empty cells (no node entry) render **nothing**. No placeholder rect, no role chip, no label — the cell is invisible.
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 4. ARROW RULES (MANDATORY)
181: 
182: Four styles, bound to topology. Connectors are drawn **before** all node rects (z-order rule).
183: 
184: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
185: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
186: | `muted` | `muted` | 1.0 | — | `arr-muted` | Standard data hand-off between steps or within a lane. |
187: | `trigger` | `muted` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arr-muted` | Governance trigger — an admin action enables downstream work. Unlabelled. |
188: | `accent` | `accent` | 1.2 | — | `arr-accent` | Focal cross-role handoff. **Exactly one per diagram**, labeled. |
189: | `link` | `link` | 1.0 | — | `arr-link` | Published / externally-consumed output. |
190: 
191: **Defs block** (required, three markers):
192: 
193: ```svg
194: <defs>
195:   <pattern id="dots" width="22" height="22" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
196:     <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="0.8" fill="{ink @ 0.10}"/>
197:   </pattern>
198:   <marker id="arr-muted"  markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{muted}"/></marker>
199:   <marker id="arr-accent" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{accent}"/></marker>
200:   <marker id="arr-link"   markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" refX="5" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="{link}"/></marker>
201: </defs>
202: ```
203: 
204: ### 4.1 Routing rules (non-negotiable)
205: 
206: - **Single-bend routing:** horizontal-first, then vertical. Exit a node from the **right edge**; enter from the **left** (same-lane horizontal) or **top/bottom** (cross-lane vertical).
207: - **No diagonals.** Bends use an 8-px Q-bezier corner.
208: - **Same-step cross-lane (vertical)**: line directly between `(step_cx(j), lane_y_top(k_to)−12)` and `(step_cx(j), lane_y_top(k_to))`. Used for admin → engineers triggers under the same step.
209: - **Cross-lane cross-step (focal)**: exit right, run horizontal past the source node's right edge to a corridor x just before the target's step, then drop vertically.
210: - **Labels:** only the `accent` arrow gets a label. Use a paper-filled rect mask (opaque) 6 px behind the text. Other arrows are unlabelled.
211: - **Z-order:** all arrows emitted before any node rect (the rect fills mask the line ends inside the node).
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE
216: 
217: Any node, lane, or step may declare an optional `color: "#hex"`. Mirrors high-level §4.4 and dp-integration §5 so the rule reads identically across types.
218: 
219: ### 5.1 Per-node `color`
220: 
221: Applied to:
222: 
223: | Element | Light | Dark |
224: |---|---|---|
225: | Container fill (`rect`) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
226: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (stroke-width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.45)` |
227: | Role chip fill | `rgba(C, 0.18)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.22)` |
228: | Role chip text | `C` | `C_light` |
229: | Title text | `C` | `C_light` |
230: | Sub-label | **unchanged** (muted) | **unchanged** (muted) |
231: | Tool label | **unchanged** (soft) | **unchanged** (soft) |
232: | Data-type chips | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
233: | Arrows touching this node | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
234: 
235: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15% for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
236: 
237: ### 5.2 Per-step `color`
238: 
239: Replaces the step header chip's fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the chip's number + label text fill with `C`. The legend's matching step entry uses the same colors.
240: 
241: ### 5.3 Per-lane `color`
242: 
243: Replaces the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` (only for odd-indexed lanes that receive a tint by default — or extend to all lanes if explicitly chosen) and the lane label text fill with `C`. Use sparingly; lane tints are easy to over-apply.
244: 
245: ### 5.4 Rules
246: 
247: - **Never on focal nodes / focal steps.** The accent already carries that signal. A `color` on a focal element is ignored.
248: - **Never on arrows.** Arrows are topology-driven. If you want a colored edge, pick a different `style` from §4, not a color override.
249: - **Cap at 3 custom-colored elements** per diagram (nodes + lanes + steps combined), in addition to the focal pair (focal node + focal step header). Above 3 the visual signal starts to fragment — if you need more, split the diagram or rethink whether each color carries distinct meaning.
250: - **Subtitles and tool labels stay muted.** Only the primary identity (border + role chip + title + icon) carries the color signal.
251: 
252: ### 5.5 Semantic palette (recommended)
253: 
254: Same palette as high-level / dp-integration so a reader scanning multiple diagrams sees the same colors meaning the same thing:
255: 
256: - `#b85450` rust-red — Security / Identity / Governance (admin nodes, LDAP, access control)
257: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — Observability / Quality (monitoring, data-quality gates, lineage)
258: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — Governance / Lineage (catalog, metadata)
259: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — Backup / DR / Archive
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
264: 
265: The data-flow diagram is built around **one cross-role handoff** that defines its central claim. Three focal slots, exactly one entry each:
266: 
267: - **One focal step** (`steps[j].focal: true`) — typically the analytical pivot (Analyze, Model, …). Header chip and legend chip both render in accent.
268: - **One focal node** (`nodes[i].focal: true`) — the node that *receives* the focal handoff. Accent border + accent role chip + ink title.
269: - **One focal arrow** (`arrows[i].style: "accent"`) — the cross-role handoff into the focal node. Solid accent stroke + labeled with a short payload descriptor (e.g., `anon data`).
270: 
271: If zero or >1 of any focal slot are declared, halt and ask the user.
272: 
273: ---
274: 
275: ## 7. DARK MODE
276: 
277: | Token | Light | Dark |
278: |---|---|---|
279: | Paper | `paper` | `ink` |
280: | Ink | `ink` | `paper` |
281: | Muted | `muted` | `soft` |
282: | Soft | `soft` | `rule-solid` |
283: | Accent | `accent` | `accent` |
284: | Link | `link` | `link` |
285: | Dot pattern | `ink @ 0.10` | `paper @ 0.10` |
286: | Lane tint | `ink @ 0.018` | `paper @ 0.025` |
287: | Dividers | `ink @ 0.12` | `paper @ 0.12` |
288: | Default chip fill | `ink @ 0.12` | `paper @ 0.12` |
289: | Focal chip fill | `accent @ 0.20` | `accent @ 0.22` |
290: | Default node fill | `paper` | `paper @ 0.04` |
291: | Default node stroke | `ink @ 0.25` | `paper @ 0.20` |
292: | Focal node fill | `accent @ 0.07` | `accent @ 0.12` |
293: | Focal node stroke | `accent` | `accent` |
294: | Custom component colors | `C` | `C_light` (lighten ~15%) |
295: 
296: ---
297: 
298: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
299: 
300: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
301: 
302: 1. `viewBox = "0 0 {viewBox_w} {viewBox_h}"` derived from `n_steps` and `n_lanes` via §3.
303: 2. Header strip at `y=0..36`; legend strip at `y=legend_y_top..viewBox_h` (`legend_y_top = 36 + n_lanes * 80`).
304: 3. Every node at `(step_cx(j) - 50, lane_y_top(k) + 8)` size `100×64`.
305: 4. Empty cells render nothing — no placeholder rect, no text.
306: 5. Exactly **one** focal step (`steps[j].focal: true`).
307: 6. Exactly **one** focal node (`nodes[i].focal: true`).
308: 7. Exactly **one** focal arrow (`style: accent`). Labeled, with a paper-masked rect behind the label.
309: 8. All other arrows unlabelled.
310: 9. All arrows emitted before any node rect (z-order rule).
311: 10. Single-bend routing only — no diagonals. Q-bezier `r=8` at each bend.
312: 11. Custom component colors ≤ 3 (in addition to the focal pair). Arrows never recolored by component `color`.
313: 12. Subtitle and tool labels stay muted regardless of any component `color`.
314: 
315: ---
316: 
317: ## 9. DATA-TYPE CHIPS REFERENCE (INPUT + OUTPUT)
318: 
319: Small `16×8 rx=3` badges at the bottom of each node, one for input and one for output. Position is **non-negotiable**:
320: 
321: - **Input chip** at `(node_x+4, node_y+54)` — bottom-**left** of the node. Represents the payload format *entering* the node from upstream.
322: - **Output chip** at `(node_x+80, node_y+54)` — bottom-**right** of the node. Represents the payload format *leaving* the node toward downstream.
323: 
324: Either chip may be omitted (e.g., a sink node has only an input chip; a source-only node has only an output chip). Reading the diagram becomes a payload-transformation trace: scan a row, read each node's input → output, and you see exactly what shape the data takes at each hand-off.
325: 
326: ### Chip codes
327: 
328: | Code | Color | Meaning |
329: |------|-------|---------|
330: | `WB` | `#6e6479` (mauve) | Web / Public data |
331: | `DB` | `#5c7899` (steel-blue) | Dataset / Raw file |
332: | `TB` | `#b8915a` (amber) | Table / Analysis-ready |
333: | `FL` | `#9c6b50` (sienna) | File / Report / Export |
334: | `LS` | `#4a7c59` (forest) | Live stream / Event |
335: 
336: Text inside chip: white, `eyebrow` role at 5px, weight 700.
337: 
338: Data-type chip colors are a **separate semantic axis** from the per-node color override (§5). The chip colors describe *payload format*; the node color override describes *concern type* (governance, observability, …). Don't conflate them — a node can have both an `out: TB` amber chip and a rust-red border color simultaneously.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## 10. LEGEND (3- OR 4-ROW STRIP)
343: 
344: Each row introduced by a category label at `x=144`. The default legend has **3 rows** (`STEPS` / `DATA TYPE` / `FLOW`); when one or more nodes carry a `color` override (§5), add a 4th `CONCERN` row and grow `legend_h` to 100 (so `viewBox_h = header_h + n_lanes·80 + 100`).
345: 
346: - **Row 1 — `STEPS`** at `y = legend_y_top + 16`: repeat the header chips with their labels. Focal step keeps accent fill.
347: - **Row 2 — `DATA TYPE`** at `y = legend_y_top + 37`: one swatch per chip type actually used in the diagram. **Append a small sub-hint** in the muted `sublabel` role after the chips: `left chip = input · right chip = output`. This makes the position-based input/output convention explicit for first-time readers.
348: - **Row 3 — `CONCERN`** (only when color overrides are present) at `y = legend_y_top + 58`: one mini-rect per custom color used, with its semantic label (e.g., `Identity · Governance`, `Data Quality · Observability`). The focal accent swatch is also shown here so the reader sees all three colored axes side-by-side.
349: - **Row 4 — `FLOW`** (last row, position depends on whether `CONCERN` row exists): short line segments with their marker + text label, one per arrow style actually used.
350: 
351: All legend items align on a single horizontal strip per row. Do not stack vertically inside a box.
352: 
353: ---
354: 
355: ## 11. COMPLEXITY BUDGET
356: 
357: | Dimension | Max |
358: |---|---|
359: | Lanes (roles) | 4 |
360: | Steps | 6 |
361: | Nodes per lane | Nodes = active steps only — empty cells are invisible (no placeholder box) |
362: | Labelled arrows | 1 (focal accent only) |
363: | Data-type chips per node | 2 |
364: | Custom-colored elements (§5) | 3 (in addition to focal node + focal step) |
365: 
366: Above 4 lanes or 6 steps: split into two diagrams (e.g., ingestion pipeline / analytics pipeline).
367: 
368: ---
369: 
370: ## 12. ANTI-PATTERNS
371: 
372: - **Placeholder empty cells** — if a role doesn't participate in a step, leave the cell empty (no box, no text).
373: - **More than one labelled arrow** — only the focal cross-role handoff gets a label.
374: - **Diagonal arrows** — always horizontal-first, then vertical; single right-angle bend.
375: - **`title` role for node titles** — node titles use the `node-name` role (technical context). Only the page `<h1>` uses `title`.
376: - **Accent on more than one node, one step, one arrow** — focal = one node + one step + one arrow, max.
377: - **`node-name` role for role labels** — lane labels always use the uppercase `eyebrow` role (they are identifiers, not prose).
378: - **`color` override on a focal element** — ignored. Accent always wins.
379: - **Custom-colored arrows** — arrows are topology-driven. Color on a node never spreads to its edges.
380: - **Lane tints over-applied** — a tint on every lane reads as decoration, not signal. Apply to ≤1 lane.
381: 
382: ---
383: 
384: ## 13. EXAMPLES
385: 
386: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow.html` — minimal light (the platform, 4-role × 5-step: Admin, Engineers, Scientists, Consumers). Gallery default.
387: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-dark.html` — same, dark skin.
388: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-full.html` — same, editorial-card frame.
389: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended.html` — exercises §5 color override: Access Control node in rust-red (governance), Clean & Stage node in slate-blue (data quality). Focal accent on Analyze step + Explore & Model node + anon-data arrow unchanged.
390: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended-dark.html` — extended pattern, dark skin.
391: - `assets/diagrams/data-flow-extended-full.html` — extended pattern, editorial-card frame.
